insight: There's been no rain at all lately, so there's no runoff driving contamination, and strong summer sunlight is helping disinfect the water. The model's main signals right now: hours since high tide is lowering risk — the timing relative to high tide affects how concentrated bacteria are at the shoreline; high tide level is raising risk — a high tide can mobilize bacteria held in wet sand and push the waterline toward outfalls; and no rain has fallen, so nothing is washing off the land into the surf. The last lab sample (5 MPN/100mL) is now 9 days old — beaches are sampled about weekly, so a reading this stale carries little weight, and this estimate leans on current conditions. It's a naturally clean, well-flushed open-coast beach (unsafe only ~3% of the time), so outside of storms it's reliably safe.
